A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MultiCrafter, with the same authors, core method, and original benchmarks. All 22 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison. V2's unresolved citations are document defects rather than missing comparison material.

before.justification: V1 reports original quantitative comparisons, component ablations, and qualitative single-subject, multi-human, and multi-object generation results.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds dataset-quality analysis, a retrained baseline, a user study, expert-routing analysis, and three-person generation experiments.

M1.justification: Attention regularization, MoE-LoRA routing, GSPO optimization, Hungarian matching, and Algorithm 1 remain equivalent. V2's two-stage description groups the existing single-subject and multi-subject training phases under fidelity pre-training; Appendix B confirms the same underlying sequence and objectives.

E1.justification: Supplement I adds training on 10,000 three-person examples and qualitative evaluation in Supplement Figure 9, extending the previously tested subject counts. Existing single-subject, two-person, and multi-object coverage remains. Naming OpenHumanVid supplies provenance for the existing video dataset rather than establishing its replacement.

E2.justification: The seven main quantitative baselines remain unchanged. Supplement D adds a separately evaluated UNO variant retrained on the authors' dataset, alongside official UNO and MultiCrafter. The three-person comparisons extend existing comparator methods to the new scenario.

E3.justification: V2 introduces substantial additional evaluation procedures: dataset-matched UNO retraining, human evaluation across five criteria, and a controlled routing comparison between left-right and top-down layouts with identities and backgrounds held constant. Existing benchmark splits and training budgets remain unchanged. Participant counts, sample counts, and rating procedures for the user study are not supplied.

E4.justification: V2 adds a training-data aesthetics distribution and retraining control to investigate the aesthetics deficit, controlled expert-routing analysis to examine layout sensitivity, and qualitative MoE ablations showing composition failures without experts. These materially expand the original component-ablation evidence in Table 2.

E5.justification: Supplement H newly reports averaging the routing-change analysis across four different seeds, with matched seeds between layout conditions. V1 has no corresponding repeated-seed analysis. Neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests for the main comparisons, and v2's user-study plot lacks uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Main Table 1 and the original metric values in Table 2 are unchanged; Table 2 adds Overall scores. New results include retrained UNO's Face-Sim of 0.2879 and AES of 0.2656, training-data mean aesthetics of 0.2552, user-study rankings, routing-change measurements, and three-person comparisons. These are additional findings under their respective settings, not improved scores on the unchanged main benchmark.

T1.justification: Supplement H introduces a layer/expert routing-change statistic, defined as |P_A-P_B|/(P_A+epsilon). V2 also omits the explicit target-velocity definition v = z0 - epsilon accompanying v1's Equation 1. The remaining optimization and matching mathematics is equivalent, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: V2 makes separation of fidelity learning and preference optimization the central contribution and stops presenting MoE-LoRA as a standalone contribution. Its conclusion explicitly claims state-of-the-art fidelity and preference alignment. The principal goal and claims of improved identity preservation and preference alignment remain.

C2.justification: V2 substantially develops the coupled-objective explanation for existing methods' failures. Supplement D attributes the aesthetics deficit primarily to training data using the retrained-UNO control, while Supplement H interprets routing changes as evidence of layout specialization. The limitations now acknowledge preliminary three-person results while retaining uncertainty about broader scalability.

D1.justification: V2 identifies OpenHumanVid as the source of the previously unspecified training videos, although its citation is unresolved. Appendix B retains the original learning rates, training steps, batch sizes, card counts, LoRA configuration, and reward weights. The renamed training stages do not establish implementation changes.

R1.justification: Related work newly contrasts training-time attention supervision with inference-time user-provided layout constraints, citing existing references such as Mix-of-Show and MS-Diffusion. V2 also prunes references, including ChatDiT and GVDiff. The overall positioning within subject-driven generation and diffusion reinforcement learning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method overview, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around objective decoupling. The separate expert-tuning subsection is merged into attention regularization, implementation descriptions are regrouped, and the supplement is reorganized. The former language-model-use disclosure is removed.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout and separately numbered supplement, recomposes the teaser and main qualitative comparison, and adds an Overall column to the ablation table. New displays include the data-quality table, aesthetics histogram, user-study chart, routing heatmap, MoE ablations, and three-person comparison. Several existing appendix figures are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the evidence through the dataset-matched UNO control and targeted MoE analyses, and partially addresses v1's untested three-person setting. These gains improve support for the paper without changing its headline results. However, the user study lacks essential protocol details, several references are unresolved, and some causal interpretations are stronger than the evidence establishes, limiting the overall improvement.
